courses.title: Introduction to Biology
courses.instructor: Seanna M. Ziehlke, Dr. Andrew C. Rush, Dr. Caitlin E. Ensign
courses.description: This lecture course provides the non-biology major with an introduction to living things and their environment. Students develop important critical thinking skills as they learn about the process of science, the building blocks of life, the role and regulation of DNA, how populations change overtime, the movement of energy within and between life forms, and how species interact with each other and their surroundings. courses.title: Latin American Literature
courses.instructor: Pauline H. Vinson, Mr. Anthony Z. Gonzales
courses.description: This course presents a variety of literary works that illuminate Latin American experiences, cultural identities, and history. Fiction, nonfiction, poetry, and other literary texts will be analyzed. This course also exposes students to distinguishing elements of selected literary formsand to the art and practice of analyzing and writing about literature. courses.title: Hist of Asian/Pacific Islander
courses.instructor: Isabella Mariano
courses.description: This course provides a comparative analysis of Asian Americans and Pacific Islanders (AAPI) history from 1848 to the present. Topics include an exploration of AAPI perspectives; immigration and settlement patterns; labor, legal, political and social history. A comparative historical approach, placing AAPI immigration within the context of global interdependence and inequality, frames the course materials. This course will examine migration theories and patterns, the politics and policies of U.S. immigration, resettlement patterns, and the reconstruction of identities and social networks. The three periods of AAPI Immigration: Before World War II; during and after World War II and the Cold War; and after 1965 to the present will be explored. CSU, UC

courses.instructor: Ms. Carmina G. Quirarte, Dr. Samantha Francois
courses.description: This course is a survey of United States history to 1877 with an emphasis on women's life experiences within the context of broader historical change. courses.title: Human Sexuality
courses.instructor: Dr. Kristen A. Colchico, Rebecca T. Ryan, DVC Staff
courses.description: This course presents an overview of the discipline of sexology from a biological, psychological, sociocultural, theoretical, and research-based perspective. Topics include the dimensions of sexuality; sex in the media including the effects of pornography; cultural variations; research methodologies; reproductive anatomy, physiology, and the sexual response system; contraception, reproduction, and reproductive options; sexually transmitted infections; sexual dysfunctions and solutions; gender; intimate relationships and communication; sexual orientation; sexual development through the lifespan; atypical (paraphilia) behaviors; violence, including rape and sexual assault; and the sexual marketplace, including human trafficking and prostitution. Students will be encouraged to examine their own sexual beliefs, values, and behaviors and cultivate unprejudiced attitudes toward diversity in human sexuality. C-ID PSY 130, CSU, UC

courses.title: The Visible Universe
courses.instructor: Mr. Paul M. Sasse, Dr. Jean E. Chiar
courses.description: This introductory course focuses on observational astronomy. Students attending in-person classes on the Pleasant Hill campus will visit the planetarium to identify constellations, discover how the rotation and orbit of the Earth affects our view of the night sky, distinguish the causes of Moon phases, and predict eclipses. Students attending online classes will view a simulated sky on their computers to identify the same motions and phenomena. Students will be introduced to light and energy output from the cosmos and use planetary orbits to find planets outside of our Solar System. CSU, UC (credit limits may apply to UC-see counselor) Prerequisite: Advisory: Placement as determined by the college's multiple measures assessment process or completion of a course taught at or above the level of intermediate algebra. Note: Students who have successfully completed ASTRO-112 should not enroll in ASTRO-110. Students who have successfully completed ASTRO-112 will not receive credit for ASTRO-110.
